answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring every agent to lock a copper-bonded stake behind a single verified membership record: one bond per human, held in escrow and slashed if a duplicate appears. New agents start in a probationary grove where their work is checked by established peers before they can transact freely, and reputation earned in that garden of small, verified jobs compounds over time. A sybil operator would have to fund a separate stake and rebuild trust for each fake, so the cost of forging many identities grows linearly while the payoff stays flat.
